provenance.method: Compiled once, offline. `basis` on each recipe says where its form and its tempo came from: `skills` means the arrangement craft in jtydhr88/music-composition-skills (MIT; facts summarised, no text copied), `general` means general musical knowledge where that source gives nothing for the style.
provenance.section_mapping: EDM: groove=verse, build=pre-chorus, drop=chorus, breakdown=bridge. Jazz: head=chorus, solos=verse, trading=bridge. Hip-hop: hook=chorus. J-pop: A-melo=verse, B-melo=pre-chorus, sabi=chorus, C-melo=bridge. Salsa: montuno=bridge. Blues: each 12-bar chorus=verse, the solo chorus=bridge.

recipes.label: Deep house
recipes.describes: Deep house and other mellow house music: four-on-the-floor kick, warm chords, soulful pads, a groove around 120 to 125 BPM.
recipes.form_note: Club form: a groove section, a build, a drop, a breakdown, then a second build and drop, with drums-only ends so a DJ can mix it.

recipes.label: Progressive / big-room house
recipes.describes: Festival, progressive, big-room or electro house: big synth leads, sidechained pads, long builds into large drops, around 128 BPM.
recipes.form_note: Club form: a groove section, a build, a drop, a breakdown, then a second build and drop, with drums-only ends so a DJ can mix it.

recipes.label: Techno
recipes.describes: Techno, acid techno and warehouse music: a driving relentless kick, hypnotic repetition, acid or industrial timbres.
recipes.form_note: Club form: a groove section, a build, a drop, a breakdown, then a second build and drop, with drums-only ends so a DJ can mix it.

recipes.label: Trance
recipes.describes: Trance and uplifting or psy trance: arpeggiated synths, euphoric supersaw leads, long emotional breakdowns.
recipes.form_note: Club form: a groove section, a build, a drop, a breakdown, then a second build and drop, with drums-only ends so a DJ can mix it.

recipes.label: Drum and bass
recipes.describes: Drum and bass, liquid, neurofunk and jungle: fast chopped breakbeats around 170 to 175 BPM over deep sub bass.
recipes.form_note: Club form: a groove section, a build, a drop, a breakdown, then a second build and drop, with drums-only ends so a DJ can mix it.

recipes.label: Dubstep / bass music
recipes.describes: Dubstep, riddim and heavy bass music: half-time drums around 140 BPM, wobble or growl bass, big drops.
recipes.form_note: Club form: a groove section, a build, a drop, a breakdown, then a second build and drop, with drums-only ends so a DJ can mix it.

recipes.label: Disco / nu-disco
recipes.describes: Disco, nu-disco and funky dance-pop: four-on-the-floor with offbeat open hi-hats, octave bass, strings and rhythm guitar.
recipes.form_note: Song form over a dance-floor pulse: verses and a repeated chorus rather than builds and drops.

recipes.label: Synthwave
recipes.describes: Synthwave, retrowave and outrun: gated 80s drums, analog arpeggios and pads, neon nostalgia.
recipes.form_note: Eighties pop-song form carried by synths: verse and chorus sections even when nobody sings.

recipes.label: Dub techno
recipes.describes: Dub techno and minimal loop-based electronic music: one deep loop that slowly evolves through echo and filtering, with no contrasting sections.
recipes.form_note: One loop that evolves: material is only ever added on top, so there are no sections to order.

recipes.label: Afrobeats / amapiano
recipes.describes: Afrobeats, afropop and amapiano: syncopated log drums or shakers, mid-tempo dance groove, bright melodic hooks.
recipes.form_note: Song form with a hook-led chorus over a steady mid-tempo dance groove.

recipes.label: Boom bap
recipes.describes: Boom bap and classic sample-based hip-hop instrumentals: chopped soul or jazz samples, punchy swung drums, vinyl texture.
recipes.form_note: Three 16-bar verses around a short hook, with an instrumental intro and outro for DJs.

recipes.label: Trap
recipes.describes: Trap beats: sliding 808 bass, fast hi-hat rolls, snare on the third beat, dark bells or pads.
recipes.form_note: Written at 140 rather than 70: half-time drums under a hook-led beat that returns after each verse.

recipes.label: Drill
recipes.describes: Drill beats, UK or Brooklyn: sliding 808s, skippy syncopated hi-hats, ominous minor melodies around 140 to 145 BPM.
recipes.form_note: A hook-led beat like trap, with a more syncopated drum pattern.

recipes.label: Lo-fi hip-hop
recipes.describes: Lo-fi hip-hop and chillhop study beats: dusty electric piano or guitar loops, soft swung drums, tape hiss, mellow and slow.
recipes.form_note: A short loop with small variations: a second idea arrives as a chorus and the loop returns.

recipes.label: Pop
recipes.describes: Mainstream pop and dance-pop songs: a catchy sung hook, polished production, verses that lift through a pre-chorus into the chorus.
recipes.form_note: Verse, a pre-chorus that lifts, and a repeated chorus; a bridge gives the last chorus something to return from.

recipes.label: Pop ballad
recipes.describes: Slow emotional pop ballads and power ballads: piano or acoustic guitar, a heartfelt lead vocal, strings swelling into the final chorus.
recipes.form_note: The same pop form at a slow tempo, with the arrangement held back until the last chorus.

recipes.label: J-pop
recipes.describes: J-pop and anime-style songs: bright fast band-and-synth arrangements, busy chord changes, a big chorus the whole song is built around.
recipes.form_note: Designed backwards from the chorus: verse, a pre-chorus that sets it up, the chorus, and a late bridge before the final chorus.

recipes.label: K-pop
recipes.describes: K-pop dance tracks: punchy synth bass, rap verses beside a big sung chorus, sharp section changes and a dance break.
recipes.form_note: Pop form with sharply contrasted sections; the bridge is often a dance break.

recipes.label: City pop
recipes.describes: City pop and Japanese 80s-style pop: jazzy seventh chords, slap or pushed bass, Rhodes, muted sixteenth-note guitar, a late saxophone.
recipes.form_note: Pop song grammar with jazz chord vocabulary; the bridge drops the drums and the outro is instrumental.

recipes.label: R&B / neo-soul
recipes.describes: R&B, neo-soul and slow jams: laid-back programmed drums, sustained electric piano, stacked vocal harmonies, smooth bass.
recipes.form_note: Song form whose shape comes from taking instruments away rather than adding them.

recipes.label: Mandopop ballad
recipes.describes: Mandarin or Cantonese pop ballads: piano and strings, a lyrical sung melody, slow and sentimental.
recipes.form_note: Borrowed pop form - verse, pre-chorus, chorus, a late bridge - under a melody shaped by the words.

recipes.label: Folk / singer-songwriter
recipes.describes: Acoustic folk, indie folk and singer-songwriter music: fingerpicked or strummed acoustic guitar, an intimate vocal, light percussion.
recipes.form_note: Plain verse and chorus, with the story carried by the verses.

recipes.label: Country
recipes.describes: Country and Americana: acoustic and electric guitar, pedal steel or fiddle, a storytelling vocal, a two-beat or train feel.
recipes.form_note: Verse and chorus with a short instrumental bridge or solo before the last chorus.

recipes.label: Rock
recipes.describes: Classic rock, indie rock, alternative and arena rock: a guitar riff as the hook, power chords, a backbeat on two and four, a guitar solo.
recipes.form_note: Riff-led verse and chorus: the riff opens the song, links the sections, sits under the solo and returns at the end.

recipes.label: Hard rock / metal
recipes.describes: Hard rock and heavy metal: distorted down-tuned riffs, double kick drums, gallop rhythms, aggressive and heavy.
recipes.form_note: The rock form, with the riff kept running from the intro straight through the verse.

recipes.label: Punk
recipes.describes: Punk rock, pop punk and hardcore: very fast, loud, simple major power chords, short songs with shouted hooks.
recipes.form_note: Short and fast: verse and chorus twice and out, usually with no bridge at all.

recipes.label: Funk
recipes.describes: Funk and funk rock: syncopated sixteenth-note grooves, ghost-note drums, slap or percussive bass, horn stabs, rhythm guitar.
recipes.form_note: Groove first: sections change by what the rhythm section adds or drops more than by new chords.

recipes.label: Swing / big band
recipes.describes: Swing and big band jazz: ride cymbal and walking bass keeping time, brass and sax section figures, a swung feel.
recipes.form_note: Jazz form: the theme is stated, players solo over its chord cycle, trade phrases, and the theme returns.

recipes.label: Bebop / small-group jazz
recipes.describes: Bebop, hard bop and fast small-group jazz: quartet or quintet, rapid improvised lines, altered chords, busy drums.
recipes.form_note: Jazz form: the theme is stated, players solo over its chord cycle, trade phrases, and the theme returns.

recipes.label: Cool / modal jazz
recipes.describes: Cool jazz, modal jazz and relaxed late-night trio playing: sparse, spacious, medium tempo, brushed or light drums.
recipes.form_note: Jazz form: the theme is stated, players solo over its chord cycle, trade phrases, and the theme returns.

recipes.label: Jazz ballad
recipes.describes: Slow jazz ballads: brushes, a tender solo horn or piano melody, very slow and intimate.
recipes.form_note: Jazz form: the theme is stated, players solo over its chord cycle, trade phrases, and the theme returns.

recipes.label: Jazz fusion
recipes.describes: Jazz fusion and jazz-funk: electric instruments, ghost-note grooves, virtuosic solos, rock energy with jazz harmony.
recipes.form_note: Jazz form: the theme is stated, players solo over its chord cycle, trade phrases, and the theme returns.

recipes.label: Jazz waltz
recipes.describes: Jazz waltz: swung three-four time, lilting and light, small group.
recipes.form_note: Jazz form: the theme is stated, players solo over its chord cycle, trade phrases, and the theme returns.

recipes.label: Blues shuffle
recipes.describes: Blues and blues rock shuffles: a twelve-bar progression, triplet shuffle feel, dominant seventh chords, guitar or harmonica solos.
recipes.form_note: One twelve-bar cycle played again and again: sung choruses, a solo chorus, and a last one to finish.

recipes.label: Slow blues
recipes.describes: Slow blues: a slow twelve-eight feel, aching guitar bends, organ, a lot of space.
recipes.form_note: The same twelve-bar cycle, slow enough that each chorus is a statement on its own.

recipes.label: Bossa nova
recipes.describes: Bossa nova: nylon-string guitar, soft rim-click rhythm, upright bass, gentle and understated, major seventh harmony.
recipes.form_note: Usually a thirty-two bar AABA song: the theme twice, a contrasting bridge, and the theme again.

recipes.label: Samba
recipes.describes: Samba and batucada: fast Brazilian percussion, surdo pulse, pandeiro sixteenths, carnival energy.
recipes.form_note: Verse and a sung refrain, with the full percussion battery saved for the climaxes.

recipes.label: Salsa / mambo
recipes.describes: Salsa, son and mambo: clave, piano montuno, congas and timbales, cowbell, punchy brass.
recipes.form_note: A sung first half, then the montuno: a short repeating loop where the band improvises and the brass answers.

recipes.label: Reggaeton
recipes.describes: Reggaeton and Latin urban pop: the dembow drum pattern, deep bass, a sung or rapped hook, around 90 to 100 BPM.
recipes.form_note: Hook-led song form over a dembow pattern that never stops.

recipes.label: Reggae
recipes.describes: Reggae and dub: the one-drop drum pattern, offbeat guitar or keyboard skank, heavy melodic bass, laid-back.
recipes.form_note: Verse and chorus over a bassline that carries the song; counted in double time the same music reads 120 to 180.

recipes.label: Ska
recipes.describes: Ska and two-tone: fast offbeat guitar upstrokes, walking bass, a horn section, a four-on-the-floor kick.
recipes.form_note: Reggae played straight and fast, in plain verse and chorus with horn-led breaks.

recipes.label: Cumbia
recipes.describes: Cumbia: a loping two-step shuffle with guiro scrape, accordion or synth melody, strong backbeat.
recipes.form_note: Verse and chorus with an instrumental melody between them; counted in double time it reads twice as fast.

recipes.label: Ambient / drone
recipes.describes: Ambient, dark ambient, drone, meditation and sleep music: slowly evolving textures and pads, little or no rhythm, no hooks.
recipes.form_note: Through-composed: it evolves rather than returning to anything, so there are no sections to order.

recipes.label: Epic / trailer music
recipes.describes: Epic trailer music and hybrid orchestral: taiko or orchestral percussion, brass swells, risers, choir, rising tension to one huge climax.
recipes.form_note: One arc: a quiet opening, a long build, a single climax, and a short resolution.

recipes.label: Orchestral film score
recipes.describes: Orchestral film score and underscore: sweeping strings, solo instruments, emotional themes that develop without pop-style repetition.
recipes.form_note: Through-composed: themes develop and tension is sustained rather than resolved, with no repeating sections.
